take_homes: Give the AI real context from your own work and the output stops being generic. Where it can't, it fills gaps with plausible typical text.
The AI's review of its own work is too kind. Treat it as a claim and trust my own knowledge, or a second independent reader, over it.
Save what worked in a rules file so the next session, or a colleague, can reuse it. That is how a habit could spread from one person to a team.

monday.move: Write down my live challenge (role design and onboarding through the pricing change) and the first source the agent could read. Before connecting any HR data, ask the DPO and the works council representative whether it is allowed.
monday.who: Me, then the DPO and one HR business partner
monday.when: Monday morning for the note, and later that week for the DPO conversation
monday.stop_condition: If the DPO says no employee data in the tool, I stay with anonymised or public material only.
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO, and I have not asked yet.

misconception.why: The module never touched jobs or headcount. It was about personal sites and rules files, so I still don't know which roles go. I do take away that AI output needs a human who knows the subject, but that is a different point.

one_line: Good idea in the middle, that the AI flatters its own work and you need to check it yourself, but I had to click past five repeats of the same boilerplate box, and nobody said what any of this means for people.
